messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: measEq.syntax not behaving as expected
parts:
This is a (trimmed) homework problem with fabricated data. There are 2 groups, and all observed variables (except the grouping variable) have 4 response categories each.
Model syntax is:

toymod<-'
f1=~y1+y2+y3
f2=~y4+y5+y6
f3=~y7+y8+y9
f2~f1
f3~f1
f2~~0*f3
'
I try to estimate the model via

toy.thresh <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = toymod, data = hw7dat2cut,
                            ordered = c(paste("y",1:9,sep='')),
                            ID.fac = "std.lv", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",
                            group = "type",group.equal=c("thresholds"),
                            return.fit=T)

and I get this in response

Higher-order factors detected. ID.fac set to "ul".
Warning messages:
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel2, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix

Data are attached.

I can sorta see how you could see a higher order factor model here, but not really--it's 3 factors with 3 indicators each. And the model is surely identified--isn't it? So I'm missing something.

Documentation says I can give measEq.syntax a fitted lavaan model. I haven't tried that yet.

Thanks.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measEq.syntax not behaving as expected
parts:
Hi Ed,

The model is fine, it just isn't purely a CFA because you have latent regressions.  Although I only noted it somewhere in fine print on the long help page, my function cannot accommodate a latent structure, except to interpret endogenous factors as indicators of the exogenous factor that predicts it (i.e., anything in Beta must be a higher-order factor loading).  You will just have to test invariance with unstructured covariances among the 3 factors, then specify a path model among the latents after (partial or full) invariance is established.  

If it is important to test invariance with the latent structure in place, then you will still have to specify the model as unstructured to use this function to write your syntax.  Then you can copy/paste the syntax into your R script and adapt it by replacing the factor covariances with directed paths.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
